title: Microsoft Teams: attendee chat in town halls for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the eDiscovery hold advice omits Microsoft's requirement for an eligible licence on every user whose content is preserved. The control paths, commands and roadmap details are supported, but conflicting Microsoft documentation about the chat default and GCC availability should also be acknowledged.

claims.claim: Town halls are events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: In events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, the chat experience differs depending on the event role.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans public event chat between all users in events larger than 1,000 users or any event optimised for a large audience.
claims.quote: All users in Events larger than 1,000 users or in any Event optimized for a large audience can now chat with one another in a public event chat in GCC, GCC High and DoD.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Meeting policy chat controls cover meetings and events up to 1,000 attendees, while large-audience attendee chat uses the events policy control.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control whether participants in your organizers' events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat messages. ... As an admin, you can manage whether organizers can turn on meeting chat for their attendees in events optimized for large audiences.

claims.claim: Meeting chat policy includes options that exclude anonymous users from reading or sending messages.
claims.quote: On for everyone but anonymous users ... All participants, except anonymous ones, can read and send chat messages.

claims.claim: The roadmap and chat guidance describe users exchanging messages, not an automated action capability.
claims.quote: Organizers can turn on Meeting chat in their Meeting options to allow attendees to send and view chat messages.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience chat experience reaches the chat control.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select the policy you want to edit or create a new one. ... In the Events optimized for a large audience chat experience dropdown list, select Optimized (the default value) or None.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None turns off the ability to enable attendee chat.
claims.quote: To turn off chat for attendees in events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None

claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate price for event chat.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams event attendee chat separate price meter licensing. Read licensing overview, attendee pack page, service description, feature comparison and returned pricing excerpts; found capacity licensing but no separate event-chat price.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery hold on the organiser's Exchange mailbox can be created in Purview, without stating the cited page's licence prerequisite.
claims.quote: eDiscovery holds require an eligible license on every user whose content you preserve. ... Placing a user on hold without proper licensing isn't supported.
claims.fix: Remove the clause '; an eDiscovery hold on the organiser's Exchange mailbox can be created in Microsoft Purview' and its link. End the sentence after 'legal hold'. This retains the verified event-chat guidance without introducing an unqualified eDiscovery licensing recommendation.

claims.claim: The act-now rating fits the standard despite an unknown arrival default and a capability organisers choose to enable.
claims.quote: action: "act-now"; defaultState: "unknown"; "Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the government-cloud release."; "organisers turn on Meeting chat in their Meeting options"
claims.fix: Set action to review. The standard assigns review to a new optional capability whose default is not stated when no source says existing behaviour changes; a near-term target alone does not establish act-now.
